newsitem.title: USA: Calif. asks Congress to respect state electric law.
newsitem.headline: Calif. asks Congress to respect state electric law.

text.p: All 52 of California's House Members jointly asked Congress on Wednesday to respect the state's plan for competition in the electricity industry.

In a letter to House Commerce Committee Chairman Thomas Bliley (R-VA), the delegation asked that any proposed federal legislation on electricity restructuring not interfere with implementation of California's own plans.
Under state legislation hammered out last summer amid heated public debate, California consumers will be able to choose their electricity supplier starting in January 1, 1998.
The law also includes a 10 percent rate reduction for residential and small business customers and contains provisions for service reliability, consumer and environmental protections.

California's three major investor-owned utilities - Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas & Electric Co, and Enova Corp's San Diego Gas & Electric Co. - have recently expressed concerns that the fragile consensus worked out in Sacramento might put them at a disadvantage in competition nationally if federal legislation is drafted.
